scenario: A site adds three new pumps to AF using the existing pump template. A PI Vision overview display shows one tile per pump using a collection whose Asset Type is the pump template.
prompt: What must the display owner do so the new pumps appear?

options.text: Nothing; a collection automatically reflects equipment added to or removed from the system
Copy and paste three more tiles and rebind them
Restart the PI Vision application pool

explanation: A collection is bound to an asset search and "automatically reflects when equipment is added or removed from the system", so matching new pumps appear on their own.

prompt: In Configure Context Switching, which option limits the Switch Asset dropdown to assets of one AF template, such as "Generic Tank Template"?
explanation: Asset Type sets the template whose elements appear for switching. Show Assets paths only changes how results are shown; the others are unrelated display settings.

prompt: You right-click an event in the PI Vision Events tab and choose Compare Similar Events by Type. What do you get?

options.text: Trends of the event's trigger attributes for that event and recent similar events
A spreadsheet export of all event frames
The display's time range set to the event

explanation: Compare Similar Events by Type trends the trigger attributes for the event and recent similar events. Setting the display time to the event is Apply Time Range.

prompt: Which criteria can you set in Edit Collection Criteria? Select all that apply.

options.text: Asset Attribute with an operator, such as > 50
The SQL query used by the PI Vision database

explanation: Collection criteria are Search Root, Return All Descendants, Asset Type and Asset Attribute conditions. The SQL database stores displays; you do not edit its queries here.

prompt: What is a pinned event in PI Vision?

options.text: A reference event saved with the display, used for example to spot batch deviations
An event that cannot be deleted from AF
An event acknowledged by an operator
An event shown on the home page

explanation: Pinned Events are reference events saved with the display and used to spot deviations, such as comparing a running batch with a good one.

prompt: True or false: every trend on a PI Vision display must use the display's time range.
explanation: False. Each trend can use the display time range, its own Duration and Offset, or a custom range such as *-48h to *.

prompt: Which features did OSIsoft list as introduced with PI Vision 2017? Select all that apply.
explanation: PI Vision 2017 introduced Collections, Drill-in Navigation, the Graphics Library, the Asset Comparison Table and User Types. OpenID Connect sign-in came much later, in the 2023 era.

prompt: What can the PI Vision XY Plot be used for? Select all that apply.
explanation: The XY Plot identifies correlations between attributes, compares assets and compares time ranges. AF templates are edited in PI System Explorer.

scenario: An analyst runs Compare Similar Events by Type on one turbine's Inactivity event, but only a few recent events from the same turbine appear. She wants to see 100 Inactivity events across all turbines.

options.text: Edit Search Criteria on the comparison

explanation: Edit Search Criteria widens an event comparison, for example to 100 Inactivity events across all turbines. Apply Time Range only sets the display time.

prompt: By what can the PI Vision Events Table filter events?

options.text: Asset type, severity, hierarchy and more
Only by the PI point's PointSource

explanation: OSIsoft's 2017 session describes the Event Table filtering by asset type, severity, hierarchy and more.

prompt: What did the PI Vision 2017 R2 Related Assets feature let display authors do? Select all that apply.

options.text: Define asset criteria for context switching
Swap a single asset or an entire asset path
Create new AF elements from the display

explanation: Related Assets let authors define criteria, swap a single asset or a whole path, or disable switching; users could filter related assets by name. Displays do not create AF elements.
